steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Stop knocking on the window sill. Are you trying to send a secret message?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: As you can see, I am unable to play my cello because it's been Arts-locked. It is... uncomfortable.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Unless you would care to join me for a chat.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Absolutely not.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Very well then. I suppose I'll have to wait for another guest.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Try anything funny, and we'll bind your arms and legs with Arts.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: My apologies, but Grimmacht has forbidden anyone from meeting with Arturia.
Not even an Empresses' Voice?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: No exceptions.
Then what about... Ewigegnade's envoy?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: ...Ewigegnade sent you?
Was that not clear enough?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Now this is a surprise.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: To think you'd be the first to come and see me.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: This is the second time we've met, Arturia.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Oh, more than that, I would think.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: How many times have we met, in the sound of music?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I see your words are as mysterious as your music. And yourself.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Me? Mysterious?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: On the contrary, I'm far more open and frank than most.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: So an Empresses' Voice, a paragon of law and order, has come to meet with a dangerous felon alone. Even going as far as to fake an empress's orders to do so... That must have taken quite a bit of determination.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You knew I wasn't sent by Ewigegnade?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: There's nothing she could possibly want to ask me. But you, Viviana, your face is full of question marks. So what would you like to know, from your former enemy?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Allow me to guess... you want to know the truth behind your father's death.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ja.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That said, I'm not used to answering questions.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Do I need to offer you something in exchange?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A trade, hm... How about you simply open yourself up to me, and allow me to search your heart?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: That's...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Oh, pardon my impertinence.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Then let's tell a story together, as usual.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Once upon a time, there was a child who lived on top of a tower in the middle of a storm.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Until the age of nine, she never left her little room in the tower.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You know my—

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Oh, don't give me that look. Like I said, this is simply a story we're telling together.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Imagine that you're a part of it, and... reach out to yourself.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Very well.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Tell me, what is it about the tower that left the deepest impression on the child?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The window.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It was a small room. The window was small, too. You could reach out and touch the cold, wet clouds.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The storms rarely abate in Sturmland, do they?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ja. Dark lightning often knocked at the window. My mother would hold me, telling stories and reading me poems in a soft, gentle voice.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What about your father?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: He... One night a week, he would come to the spire where I lived, bringing me books and teaching me to play instruments.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You looked forward to these meetings. Did you leave your room and wait for him at the top of the staircase, when it was almost time?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: When I was little. But I stopped.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The skies were very dark that day. It had been a long time my father's last visit. I was out of candles, and I wanted to find some, so I went further than I usually did.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I saw so many children and adults. The music combined with their laughter was louder than the thunder.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That's when you realized that not every child had to stay in their room like you did. That they could hold their parents' hands, and dance and sing to their hearts' delight.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Did you see your father there? Did you look for him?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I wanted to, but my mother pulled me back. She covered my ears, and tried to cover my eyes too... It hurt a bit, but I didn't dare say anything.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: She brought you back to your little room. Did you look up?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Nein. I... I kept my eyes closed. I heard my mother crying, but I didn't dare look at her.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Didn't dare?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Ja. I didn't dare go down the stairs. I didn't dare look for my father anymore.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I never looked up again, even after my mother passed away, when my father sent me away from the spire.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Why not?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: My father was a Kurfürst. He and my mother weren't married. My existence was a secret that would hurt my mother and make things difficult for my father if anyone found out.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: No, that's not what I'm asking. How did you feel?

spans.text: No, that's not what I'm asking. How did

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You were the one trapped in the spire. You were the one forbidden to recognize your father. You were the one who watched your mother waste away. You were the one sent away from home.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: When you went to Kazimierz and decided to become a knight, you held a sliver of expectation.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: After all, the stories of your childhood, the stories about knights, had long been your source of comfort.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But you soon realized you were no more than a puppet of the General Chamber of Commerce.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Even your childhood in the spire was boiled down to an exotic label. 'The Leithanian.' An advertisement destined to sell in the markets of both countries.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You left the arena after getting on the wrong side of the KGCC. You thought you would finally have some peace and quiet, only to be summoned back to Leithanien by a letter from your father.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Once again, you find your fate written by another. Illegitimate child, competition knight, Empresses' Voice. You never chose any of these identities.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And it all started on that spire, at the top of those stairs.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...You're right.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's been so many years, but sometimes I feel like I'm still there.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Like I never left it.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Once again, think back to the memory that left the deepest impression.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That day, when your father took your hand and descended the seemingly endless stairs... You didn't look up.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I couldn't.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: If I did, he would see the tear stains on my face, and the tears in my eyes...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Anger.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: 'I already lost my mother. Why are you pushing me away like this?'

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ja. I had... nothing.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Why abandon me?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I already lost my mother. Why did I have to lose my father too?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Why couldn't you have waited in Marigold Alley just a little longer?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Why did you write for me to come back, only to leave me again once I'd returned with hope in my heart?
Arturia does not answer.
She simply gazes at Viviana, at the ripples in the lake of her eyes.
If silence can be considered an expression of sound, then their emotions could resonate even without a melody.
Anger, frustration, pain. The same emotions reflected in Arturia's eyes.
She sighs, and awakens the dreamer from her memory with gentle words.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That's enough storytime.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Kurfürst Werner was my friend, Viviana.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Our meeting was so ordinary that it's hardly worth mentioning. He was a high noble, but also a sensitive and romantic artist. We often spoke about music.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A few months ago, his envoy found me while I was traveling.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: He knew his days were numbered. All he wanted was to see his beloved again, through my music.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: He wanted to see Mother?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Not just Lucinda, but you as well.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Werner did reminisce about his romance with Lucinda, but he spent even more time in that little room on the spire.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Those nights with you and your mother were his only comfort in those painful early days as Kurfürst.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That's how I knew your story.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So it wasn't...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: No, I did not use Arts on you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I'd already met you countless times, through Werner's mind's eye.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You must hear this often, but you really are so much like your father.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But it was only when I saw you in person that I realized...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You're more than just that flickering candle.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: More than... what?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You're so much stronger, so much tougher than a candleflame.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Now, I've told you everything I could.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Kurfürst Werner died over the copy of the Güldenesgesatz. On that matter, you know as much as I do.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...You told me he knew his end was coming. Which means he knew how he would die.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Protecting the Güldenesgesatz was his vow to the Twins, and his duty as Kurfürst of Sturmland.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Whether it was the Movement or its loss, the responsibility and blame lie solely on Sturmland.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Only by giving his life for it could he protect his loved ones and House Hochberg, all while ridding himself of a ticking time bomb.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It was all for the Güldenesgesatz?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I think... I understand.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: One last bit of advice, to thank you for your trust and sincerity.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: When I first saw you, I also saw the shadow behind you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But now, it's growing, filling the entire staircase outside.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Danke, Arturia... for the answers.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: My dear Viviana... How pitiable, how noble...

spans.text: My dear Viviana... How pitiable, how

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Will you be swallowed by the shadow?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Whew, made it.

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: You move so quickly, Herr Erich, I could hardly keep up.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Pardon my excitement. I thought I wouldn't be able to leave Sturmland, but the Empresses' Voice delayed the visit.

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: Kurfürsten succession ceremonies rarely take this long, not since the reign of the Witch King...

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Stop worrying. While in Zwillingstürme, what could be more important than seeing Their Majesties?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Hurry, and we may even secure a seat closer to the Twin Spires before anyone else arrives... Hey, why is that man not moving?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Guten Tag!

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Are you here for Das Kaiserinnensfest too?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I suppose so.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Where is your instrument, then? What are you going to do for the ensemble?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The ensemble?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: The ensemble of the Güldenesgesatz! The most important part of the ceremony, bathing in the glory of both the Golden Melody and Leithanien!

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: This is my master's first time attending. I have his flute with me.

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: Ah, of course. Do forgive my nosiness. Which Kreis do you hail from?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Does it matter?

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: Oh, no, I don't mean to pry, only that it's customary for those from the same Kreis to stand together.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I see. Please, go ahead. We will follow.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Oh, very good then! I mean, danke, meine Herr. May Grimmacht's glory and Ewigegnade's blessings orbit you like the sun.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Seeing the Twin Empresses' spires for the first time?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The white dress of Ewigegnade, the Eternal Grace.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The black blade of Grimmacht, the Austere Authority.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Their two spires resemble them so very much.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The Twin Spires are Zwillingstürme's namesake. They're the pride of Leithanien.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No matter how beautiful, they're no more than two elaborate cages.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: An apt metaphor.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Das Kaiserinnensfest... They say it's for all Leithanians, but only nobles are allowed to join in the ensemble at the amphitheater.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: It is, in effect, a performance of an Arts ritual.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: A ritual?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Did you see the bridge connecting the spires?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: That's where the Twin Empresses play every year. The sound of the pipe organ and violin are amplified by the resonance between the buildings, spreading to every corner of Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So it's some kind of... Arts.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The old man told me that it's the work of Herkunftshorn. He turned Vedunien into a massive Arts device, with the bell tower of Weinshof at the center.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: And the Twin Empresses have built upon the Witch King's Arts.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: To avoid making the same mistake as him, they set the Twin Spires as the center of the resonance, effectively tuning the entire city and making it virtually impossible to assail the Spires from the outside.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Anyone wanting to attack the Kaiserinnen will either need to destroy the entire palace area where the Spires are located, or work from within.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Spoken like someone who's given some thought to planning such an attack.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Wait, don't tell me you actually—

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If we see the Gendarmerie or the Empresses' Voice, remind me to run faster than you.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: ...Quiet.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The celebration is about to begin. People are coming, try to blend into the crowd. Don't just stand there like earlier.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What about when the ensemble begins? We didn't bring any instruments, unless your sword is a fair bit more versatile than it looks.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: If the ensemble begins.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I met that distant relative of yours.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Exactly as you predicted, she offered a generous lead.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Perhaps we really are trapped in some kind of illusion they created.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: What if the Witch King's remnants aren't trying to use the Güldenesgesatz to get to the Witch King's legacy, but to use the Witch King's powers to tamper with it?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: What if their goal has never truly changed?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: ...What are you still doing here, meine Dame?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: All the Empresses' Voices in Zwillingstürme have been summoned to the amphitheater.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ah, I was... I'll be on my way.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Hm, this cell holds a dangerous felon, and it is quite far from the amphitheater. I'll need to contact Grimmacht's...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I would not recommend that.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: A Sankta?! What's a Sankta doing here?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Let's catch him together, meine Dame! He may well be in league with Arturia!

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Nngh?!

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Sorry.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I was about to ask your opinion on how to handle this.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So if I weren't here, you would have simply done it yourself?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: My presence here already violates diplomatic protocol. An additional rule being broken is of little consequence, other than in terms of the subsequent clean-up.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are an Empresses' Voice. Michael has told me of your circumstances.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I appreciate your kind gesture.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It was my own decision to visit Arturia.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I didn't want my father's death to be meaningless.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I didn't want to keep my head down and pretend nothing had happened.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I wanted to fight for something, to finally seize my own fate with my two hands.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...You chose to let Arturia perform your heart's music?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Nein.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The melody was always there, echoing in my heart. I just chose not to listen to it until now.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I believe she's telling the truth that the Güldenesgesatz is at the heart of the problem.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Imperial casters have recovered the copy of Güldenesgesatz.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: However, I have learned that Arturia has an accomplice with whom she was in close contact. The available evidence indicates that this person may not have been the mastermind behind the Ludwigs-Universität incident.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Hm... then we can assume that the Witch King's remnants have already obtained the Arts recorded in the copy.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The Güldenesgesatz will be performed by over ten thousand people at the amphitheater.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: If the Witch King's remnants are in that crowd... the consequences will be unimaginable.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I would like to share our current findings with Michael.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Sure. He might be able to persuade Grimmacht.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But that's not enough. We must take action ourselves... even without Their Majesties permission.

steps.name: Imperial Musician
steps.text: The musicians and instruments are in position, Frau Löwenstein.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Very well. Give me a moment while I double-check the amplification Arts.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You're back, Amelie? Did you forget something?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: No need to be nervous. This is your first public performance as part of the orchestra. Just hold your instrument steady and focus on the melody. Pay no mind to anyone watching.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Oh... it's you.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Adjust the direction of that Arts Unit, will you? Turn it counterclockwise 15... 17 degrees.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Ja, that's how it should sound. But why are you here at this hour? Is Ewigegnade still concerned about the effect on the performance?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Frau Löwenstein... where are the other musicians?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: At the amphitheater.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The performance of the Güldenesgesatz will begin in ten minutes. The Reichsorchester needs a good start under the direction of the Kaiserin.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Only ten minutes?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The Kaiserin's weather casters have forecasted the exact time of today's sunset. As per custom, the performance of the Güldenesgesatz will conclude just as the last ray fades.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The rehearsal schedule has been hard, but we'll be able to rest once we get through this evening.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You too, Viviana. I've been thinking... You'll need to find a long-term residence in Zwillingstürme, if you're to remain by the Kaiserin's side when this all over.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Would you like to stay at my place?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I have a little mansion in Bachshof. I just had the walls repainted.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Brandt planted some vines, which he says goes well with the walls. But to be honest, I'd like a second opinion before I commit.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Frau Löwenstein... Cora.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Ja? What is it?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: How might one stop the performance of the Güldenesgesatz?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Why do you ask? This performance has been the most important part of Das Kaiserinnensfest for the last twenty-three years. So many people are waiting in the amphitheater in front of the Spires.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I've almost gotten to the bottom of these tragedies.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I'm sure the enemy's plan has something to do with the Güldenesgesatz. They cannot be allowed to succeed.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: And how did you learn this? Have you told Ewigegnade?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I don't know who to trust... I can't stop thinking about who killed my father.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You suspect Their Majesties? You're an Empresses' Voice, Viviana!

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Who's there?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: A friend. He's keeping watch.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The empresses' casters are coming.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So soon?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It will take more than ten minutes to neutralize them.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The performance of the Güldenesgesatz is about to begin.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Don't fight them.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I'll be with you, Viviana, no matter what you do.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You believe me?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Do you even need to ask? Besides, I can't let you put yourself in danger.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You want to stop the Reichsorchester from playing the Güldenesgesatz, right? I'll take you there.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: ...They've gone out.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The candles on the stairs. The room is so much darker now, don't you think?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: What are you doing? Stay away from the door.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: There are less people out there now.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Have they... gone after that lovely Empresses' Voice?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Frau Hochberg is suspected to have fallen under your influence. She will be taken into custody until the conclusion of the celebration.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: It was a mistake to allow her to meet with you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A mistake, you say?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You knew the new Empresses' Voice was the daughter of a Kurfürst, and had the favor of Ewigegnade.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Compared to working in Grimmacht's dark Spire, you clearly show more interest in its twin, the white Spire.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: So you let the empress's new favorite come in without the proper checks, just to curry favor with her.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Wh-What are you babbling about?!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But you soon realized the danger. Let me guess: Viviana did something unbefitting of her status after she left, didn't she?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Now you're afraid. Grimmacht and her executors will not tolerate such a gross error. You would lose any chance of promotion, perhaps even your freedom.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: So why did you make a second mistake, then?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Wha... music! How can this be?!

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Grimmacht, please... Nein, spare me! I-I can't listen...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Too late. There are just too many instruments in Leithanien. Your Arts Units, like your souls, are laid bare before me.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Your kn-knocking...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You dared not carry your instruments with you in my presence, so you left them outside the door. But in your haste, you forgot the protective Arts.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You forgot that vibrations can be transmitted.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The tiniest tremor of a string, and you're hearing my music.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Check my crown, would you?

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Ja.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Your fingers are cold.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Sorry. How about this? That better?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You've been clutching your sword all day. Its chill has rubbed off on you.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: ...It's time. We should head to the bridge.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Hildegard...

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Ja? What is it?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Am I pretty today?

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: As always.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Grimmacht!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: ...Ewigegnade.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Your wolf cub is here.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Go first, Lieselotte. The people are waiting.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: We've always walked out onto the bridge together.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Nothing is obliged to stay the same forever.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: I'll find you before the performance begins.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: So why are you here? I thought you preferred it down below.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I have an urgent matter to report.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Bring my violin. We'll talk on the way.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Nein!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Please, you must order the celebration to be halted. The Witch King's remnants are in the crowd, planning a massive attack!

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Proof?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: ...Please, just give me a little time. I'll find the proof.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: You didn't use to be so brash, Michael. That reckless Sankta has changed you.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Federico... the Lateran executor believes that a larger incident is in the works, and it has something to do with Arturia. We should interrogate her!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: What does she know about the Güldenesgesatz, who are her supporters, what are she and her accomplices planning... As long as the performance of the Güldenesgesatz can be delayed, I can—

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: I see you believe the Celebration to be a mere festivity.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: The 'Kaiserinnensfest' first took place twenty-three years ago, on the day we killed the Witch King.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: But there were no empresses, and no celebration, only soldiers fallen in battle, and a tired and frightened people.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: We defeated the Witch King in the early dawn, and spent the next few hours cleaning up his followers. At dusk, Lieselotte and I descended the Spire, walked down its bloody steps, and—

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Announced our victory with a duet.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Today, the ten thousand people of the ensemble come from every Kreis, from all four corners of Leithanien.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Every Leithanian, every friend of Leithanien, and every enemy of Leithanien has their eyes on the Twin Spires. On Grimmacht and Ewigegnade.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: And you want me to suspend, even cancel, the ensemble based on the hypothesis of a Lateran executor who has already caused his fair share of trouble in our country.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Perhaps I expected too much of you.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: You should have known I would respond like this before you even spoke. And if you truly believed in your judgment, you should have acted on your own.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: On that account, the daughter of Werner von Hochberg is far more resolute than you.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: How long have you been with me, Michael?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Seven years.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: It's time to let you go.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: What? Why would you say that?

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: There comes a day when one must shoulder more responsibility, for the sake of Leithanien's future.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Bring me my violin. It's time I went to the bridge.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The orchestra is ten meters below us.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The sun has... painted the clouds red.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Three minutes, fifty seconds until the performance begins.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I will fire a blank. The noise should cause some of the musicians to scatter and interrupt the performance.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The musicians of the Reichsorchester are all Arts masters, each one the equal of an Empresses' Voice. We would be drowned in Arts the moment you showed an intent to attack.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The equivalent of ninety-seven Empresses' Voices, then.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Plus two squads of approaching casters, for a total of one hundred twenty.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...I can give you three minutes.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You must secure the remaining twenty-three seconds on your own, Seniora Hochberg.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Three minutes? But if this is the only way...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Delay the casters. Leave the rest to me.
The shadows of the Twin Spires stretch as the sun sinks towards the horizon.
They swallow up the shadows of the musicians, of Cora, of Viviana herself.
She has never felt her power unleashed like this.
She is reminded of that flickering candlelight in the spire.
It was a tiny flame that only illuminated a corner of the bed. Leaving the other corners, the spiral staircase, and the night beyond the spire in total darkness.
There was a time when she couldn't admit that the darkness would linger in her eyes longer than that tiny speck of candlelight.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Success.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I cut off the connection between some of the musicians and their instruments.

steps.name: Imperial Musician
steps.text: What's going on? We're being affected by somebody's Arts.

steps.name: Imperial Musician
steps.text: You... Frau Löwenstein? Are you being held hostage?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You could say that.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: ...Nein.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I'm sorry, Amelie.

steps.name: Imperial Musician
steps.text: You're in league with each other?!

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I made my choice, and I will not hesitate.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Could you please... just put down your instrument for a while?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: There are fluctuations of Arts energy coming from below the Twin Spires... and some commotion from where the orchestra is.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The Witch King's remnants?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Possibly.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Strange. There should be Gesatzswächter in the area, but I don't see any. Why?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The Kaiserinnen knew that something terrible would happen here. They're prepared to abandon the Twin Spires if necessary. They'll even abandon all the—

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Meine Herr!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...You were from Sturmland, ja?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Why do you look like someone spooked you? The ensemble is about to begin. Here, I have an extra flute. You can borrow it.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: A flute?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: This performance is not to be missed!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Nein, you can't be here.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Go! Leave the amphitheater!

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: You'd like a better position? I suppose we could squeeze—

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm not—Do not you see these?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: See what?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The dice I'm holding! My Arts Unit!

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: What are you doing? You'll give yourself away!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Does it even matter, at this point?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Look around. There must be ten thousand people here... No, we can't even worry about that now. All we can do is save as many as we can. Even just one more...

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: It's too loud here!

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: I can't hear a word you're saying!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Look at me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Look at my Arts. Do they remind you of anything? I am an Urtica. My Arts come from the same lineage as him. You should be afraid! Run!

spans.text: Look at my Arts. Do they remind you of anything? I am an Urtica. My Arts come from the same lineage as

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Amazing! Do you hear that? The Imperial musicians just played the first note!

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: The performance of the Güldenesgesatz has begun!
The black Arts orb rises from his hand and into the air, exploding into a reddish black shadow.
It is quickly buried by even more brilliant rays of Arts.
Rays created by various Originium Arts interweave in the clouds.
Both the melody and the Arts come from the people on the ground, all focused on performing the music belonging to Leithanien alone, using instruments that also serve as Arts Units.
Even the buildings resonate with the Twin Spires, turning the empty space around the Kaiserinnen's towers into a true amphitheater.
The colors penetrating the clouds continue to shift with the splendid melody, as though the crowd is performing the color of the sunset in the sky.
It is a feast of sight and sound, woven together by Arts. The ultimate expression of Leithanien's classical aesthetics and mastery over Arts.
It is a grand spectacle visible from any corner of Zwillingstürme, and beyond.
Tears begin to fill Ebenholz's eyes.
He remembers standing atop the spire of Urtica, gazing down at the plate below.
There were many bell towers in the Grafschaft, which sang every day at dusk.
The people would leave their workshops after a long day of work, and the sound of wheels rolling over metallic roads would echo with the music filling the city.
He could see the green-black wilderness, if he stood on his toes. Einwald was filled with forests, and caravans brought ripe fruit into the city whenever they were in season.
Farmers often amplified their scents with Arts to attract customers. He could always smell the best fruits, even from his high perch.
The maid who sympathized with him would sneak a few back from the market, as long as no other nobles were watching.
The fruits were ripe and fresh, unlike the carefully selected, dried and withered food served on the long, old table.
He could not remember what became of the maid. Did she go join her beloved in the south? Or did she find a new job at the instrument workshop beneath the spire?
And, when he left Urtica... did he ever look back?
Yes, he had once loved this place from the bottom of his heart.
Leithanien, the land of divine music, cradle of the Arts.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The performance has begun.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It sounds so harmonious, even without the strings.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: There's a theory I've heard, though I've never tried to verify it.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The Güldenesgesatz contains the will of Leithanien.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: It represents order, harmony, and beauty.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The golden melody is deeply rooted in the soul of every Leithanian, and is not so easily damaged.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That sounds like a form of Originium Arts. It shares some characteristics with our law, but works on different principles, and on a different target.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So... the Güldenesgesatz is actually a kind of complex Arts affecting the cognition of every Leithanian who hears it?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Cast by... more than ten thousand people in ensemble.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So we can't disrupt the performance, but what about the enemy? What's their plan?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The enemy's plan is undoubtedly the opposite.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: They want the music to continue. Therefore, there is only one place they can be hiding.

steps.name: Imperial Musician
steps.text: Wh-What are you doing?

steps.name: Imperial Musician
steps.text: I put down my cello as you asked!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Frau Hochberg and I have not prevented any musician from leaving.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your colleagues are either resisting her Arts, or chose to avoid confrontation due to Frau Löwenstein's presence.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are the only one to have stayed behind.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Very astute, Sankta.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: We have waited far too long to hear the music that truly belongs to Leithanien.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The other Witch King's remnants are amongst the musicians?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Stay away from them, Cora!

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Are you... crying?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I'm listening to the Güldenesgesatz.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The Movement?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: It's just so beautiful.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: It reminded me of how much I used to love Leithanien.
